page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware accelerators. The underlying Intel Xeon processor provides a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography instructions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2-standard-4 delivers modest computational throughput. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall within the bottom 25% of tested instances. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measuring 27.03 GB/sec and 23.09 GB/sec respectively, placing these metrics in the bottom 25%. While single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core scores achieve average tier rankings, multi-threaded operations show notable performance drops. For example, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falls into the bottom 10%, and Geekbench image processing is also in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-4 offers a standard resource density profile suitable for entry-level enterprise workloads that do not demand high-throughput parallel processing or massive memory footprints. Given the lack of local storage and moderate database operation benchmarks, this instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and general-purpose utility workloads. It is less optimal for data-intensive tasks, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, where its low multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth would present significant bottlenecks.
